task.title: Scale guarded L12 dispatcher authoritative state reads
task.phase: Twelve Loop Current Gap / Dispatcher Prerequisite

scope.owned_layer: Guarded dispatcher authoritative state/readback snapshots, strict observational existing-authority locking, bounded-memory prefix hashing and record-wise tail replay, deterministic integrity/atomicity regressions, and task-scoped scale evidence.
scope.not_changing: No immutable 28-task catalog bytes, config, canonical journal/checkpoint, provider policy, runtime state, worker process, product controller, task materialization, service, or deployment.

baseline.root_cause: Dispatcher materialized every historical event with load_events and then revalidated the event list again through project_latest_state.

scale_benchmark.admission_verdict: failed_closed: live nonterminal artifact overlap is not dependency-ordered: L12-CONTROLLER-BFF-20260731 <-> LIFECYCLE-PROJ-BFF-001

integrity_regressions: Warm checkpoint plus empty tail reports checkpoint_used=true and zero revalidated events.
Warm, stale-tail, missing, and corrupt checkpoint dry-runs preserve the directory listing plus journal, projection, checkpoint, and lock bytes and stat identity.
Observational reads require an existing non-symlink parent, regular journal, and regular lock; missing parent/event/lock and symlink authority fail closed without creating entries.
Observational shared locking uses a read-only descriptor with no O_CREAT or fchmod, including when the provisioned lock has mode 0640.
A mutation-capable snapshot with one appended valid tail validates exactly that event and refreshes the checkpoint.
A concurrent writer waits for the snapshot reader and both observe whole journal generations.
Forced full replay matches accelerated event count, head identity, state, and state SHA.
Edited or truncated history cannot be accepted from a stale checkpoint.
Unreadable and internally valid forged checkpoints fall back to full replay and cannot substitute state.
Tail sequence and previous-event hash mismatches raise before projection.
Short append readback raises instead of accepting partial bytes.
Injected assign or sync failures leave zero catalog tasks in the canonical journal/projection.
